rationale: Time: Each iteration halves [lo, hi), so the number of iterations is O(log n). Space: Only scalar indices and the midpoint are retained.
space_rationale: Only scalar indices and the midpoint are retained.

assumptions: n = len(collection); worst-case input; comparisons and indexed accesses are O(1). Exclude the mutated input collection and returned alias.
rationale: Time: On reverse-sorted input, shifts sum to 1 + 2 + ... + (n-1), giving O(n^2) worst-case time. Space: The algorithm sorts in place and keeps only scalar temporaries.
space_rationale: The algorithm sorts in place and keeps only scalar temporaries.

assumptions: n is node count, h is tree height; count work inside the generator chain and each traversal next() call, excluding only consumer work after a value is returned; worst-case arbitrary finite binary tree is scored. Exclude the input tree and streamed output values; include active generator frames.
rationale: Time: For each yielded value at depth d, next() resumes the active yield-from delegation chain through O(d) generators. Summed over all nodes this is O(sum depth)=O(n*h); a skewed tree has O(n^2) total delegation work, while a balanced tree has O(n log n). The Python yield-from proposal explicitly notes that delegation chains in recursive traversals can make an intended O(n) operation O(n^2). Space: The recursive generator delegation retains O(h) active generator frames; a skewed tree has h = n.
space_rationale: The recursive generator delegation retains O(h) active generator frames; a skewed tree has h = n.
time_rationale: For each yielded value at depth d, next() resumes the active yield-from delegation chain through O(d) generators. Summed over all nodes this is O(sum depth)=O(n*h); a skewed tree has O(n^2) total delegation work, while a balanced tree has O(n log n). The Python yield-from proposal explicitly notes that delegation chains in recursive traversals can make an intended O(n) operation O(n^2).

assumptions: m = len(str1), n = len(str2), N = m+n; score worst case over string-length pairs with total N; scalar/cell operations are O(1). m and n are string lengths; N=m+n; exclude input strings and returned LCS; include the DP table and temporary character arrays.
expected_time_exact: O(m*n), worst case O(N^2) where N=m+n
rationale: Time: The DP table fills Θ(m*n) cells. With total input length N=m+n, this is O(N^2) in the worst case and Θ(N^2) for similarly sized strings. Splitting and traceback are linear and dominated. Space: The int table has (m+1)(n+1) cells; String[] character arrays add O(m+n), and output storage is excluded.
space_rationale: The int table has (m+1)(n+1) cells; String[] character arrays add O(m+n), and output storage is excluded.
time_rationale: The DP table fills Θ(m*n) cells. With total input length N=m+n, this is O(N^2) in the worst case and Θ(N^2) for similarly sized strings. Splitting and traceback are linear and dominated.

assumptions: One call on a fresh instance; V reachable nodes, E child references; n=V+E for the coarse class; child iteration/addAll is O(degree); expected O(1) hash/equality operations. Exclude input graph; include the retained visited list/set and pending queue; one call on a fresh instance; n=V+E for coarse class.
rationale: Time: Each distinct value is expanded at most once, so adjacency lists are processed once in total and at most E child entries are enqueued. HashSet operations are expected O(1). Dedupe by value can reduce traversal work, not increase this upper bound. Space: The retained visited list and set use O(V); because nodes are marked when dequeued, pending queue entries can total O(E).
